newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan spring crop growth at par with '92/96.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan spring crop growth at par with '92/96.

text.p: Saskatchewan spring crop growth was rated at parity with the five-year 1992/96 average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.
"On average, 65 percent of the spring cereals are at or past the tillering stage at this time of year," it said.
The cool spring slowed development of fall cereals which lagged behind the five-year average with 58 percent at or past the heading stage versus 70 percent in the five-year average.
"Winds and rain hampered spraying activity in many areas of the province. Weed growth is prolific and timely spraying is becoming a concern," it said.

An average 19 mm (0.7 inch) of rain fell on the southern grainbelt although Admiral in the west saw 75 mm (3 inches). Dry weather stressed crops in the southeast, however, while some southwestern areas reported localized flooding due to heavy rainfall.

Central Saskatchewan reported an average of 17 mm (0.7 inch) of rain, but Conquest in the west saw 60 mm (2.362 inch). Weather related crop damage was caused by drought, wind, hail and flooding, it said.
Flea beetles caused problems in canola and mustard across the region. Diamondback moths and grasshoppers were reported.

Northern districts saw an average 21 mm (0.8 inch) of rain as Paddockwood in the centre saw 40 mm (1.6 inches). There were some reports of drought, wind and flood damage. Flea beetles were reported in some areas.
